domains.details: This family represents the RNA-directed RNA polymerase found in many positive strand RNA eukaryotic viruses. Remdesivir, a recent treatment approved for Covid-19 disease, directly interacts with this region of the RdRp (NSP12) from SARS-CoV-2 and explains its mechanism of action via delayed-chain termination [[cite:PUB00099876]].
This family includes RNA helicases thought to be involved in duplex unwinding during viral RNA replication. Members of this family are found in a variety of single stranded RNA viruses.
This is a family of capsid proteins found in positive stranded ssRNA viruses such as cricket paralysis virus (CRPV). It forms an all beta sheet structure [[cite:PUB00035375]].

domains.details: This V domain of L RNA-polymerase carries a new motif, GxxTx(n)HR, that is essential for mRNA cap formation. Nonsegmented negative-sense (NNS) RNA viruses, Mononegavirales, cap their mRNA by an unconventional mechanism. Specifically, 5'-monophosphate mRNA is transferred to GDP derived from GTP through a reaction that involves a covalent intermediate between the large polymerase protein L and mRNA. The V region is essential for this process [[cite:PUB00061985]].

Members of the Mononegavirales including the Paramyxoviridae, like other non-segmented negative strand RNA viruses, have an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase composed of two subunits, a large protein L and a phosphoprotein P. This is a protein family of the L protein. The L protein confers the RNA polymerase activity on the complex. The P protein acts as a transcription factor [[cite:PUB00000746]].

domains.details: This V domain of L RNA-polymerase carries a new motif, GxxTx(n)HR, that is essential for mRNA cap formation. Nonsegmented negative-sense (NNS) RNA viruses, Mononegavirales, cap their mRNA by an unconventional mechanism. Specifically, 5'-monophosphate mRNA is transferred to GDP derived from GTP through a reaction that involves a covalent intermediate between the large polymerase protein L and mRNA. The V region is essential for this process [[cite:PUB00061985]].

Members of the Mononegavirales including the Paramyxoviridae, like other non-segmented negative strand RNA viruses, have an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase composed of two subunits, a large protein L and a phosphoprotein P. This is a protein family of the L protein. The L protein confers the RNA polymerase activity on the complex. The P protein acts as a transcription factor [[cite:PUB00000746]].
